Checking data against a specification

Source: vignettes/checking-data.Rmd
checking-data.Rmd

ysx_check() extends yspec::ys_check() with three checks that are driven by the dots of each column in the specification:

Check dots setting Default
Missing values na_ok false: missing values are not allowed
Rows per group group, pre_grp_count each group occurs once
Time-varying columns group, time_varying constant within each group

Missing values must be coded as the specification’s missing_code (SETUP__: missing_code) when one is set.

library(yspecx)

spec <- yspec::ys_select(ysx_load_pkpdspec(), ID, TIME, EVID, DV, CMT)

data <- data.frame(
  ID = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
  TIME = c(0, 1, 2, 0, 1),
  EVID = c(1, 0, 0, 1, 0),
  DV = c(-999, 5.1, 4.2, -999, 6.3),
  CMT = c(1, 2, 2, 1, 2)
)

The bundled specification marks ID as the group column and sets pre_grp_count: ~ (null), because a NONMEM data set has many rows per subject. DV allows missing values, coded as -999.

Run all checks 

ysx_check(data, spec)
#> The data set passed all checks.

ysx_check() returns TRUE invisibly when everything passes. If any check fails it prints every problem and stops. Use error_on_fail = FALSE to get FALSE back instead.

bad <- data
bad$CMT[2] <- -999
ysx_check(bad, spec, error_on_fail = FALSE)
#> The data set passed all checks.
#> Additional check messages:
#>   - CMT: 1 missing value(s) found but na_ok is not true (default)

Before it runs any check, ysx_check() asserts that the data and the specification match: every column in data must be a variable in the specification, and every specification variable must be a column in data. With the default error_on_fail = TRUE a mismatch raises an error. With FALSE it is reported with the other problems, and error_on_fail is also forwarded to the individual checks. ysx_check_missing() is less strict: it only requires the data columns to be in the specification.

Missing values

ysx_check_missing() runs only the missing-value check and returns the problems as a character vector. Every column in data must be described in the specification, otherwise it raises an error (or returns a problem with error_on_fail = FALSE). The specification may describe more columns than the data has.

ysx_check_missing(bad, spec)
#> [1] "CMT: 1 missing value(s) found but na_ok is not true (default)"

Missing values are not allowed by default. Allow them for a column with dots: {na_ok: true} in the YAML. If the specification has a missing_code, a plain NA is a problem even when na_ok is true.

A second specification can be merged before checking with spec2. Columns that exist in both keep the definition from spec.

ysx_check_missing(
  data[c("ID", "DV")],
  yspec::ys_select(spec, ID),
  spec2 = yspec::ys_select(spec, DV)
)
#> character(0)

Repeats within groups

ysx_check_repeats() counts the rows in each group and stops if any group does not have exactly count rows (default 1). It is the equivalent of grouping, counting, and checking that no count differs from count. Missing values count as a group value.

Pass the grouping columns with groups to avoid editing the specification. The columns must exist in the specification.

ids <- data.frame(ID = c(1, 1, 2), TIME = c(0, 0, 0))
ysx_check_repeats(ids, spec, groups = c("ID", "TIME"))
#> Error:
#> ! 1 of 2 group(s) defined by ID, TIME do not have 1 row(s) (row counts found: 2)

With error_on_fail = FALSE the problems are returned instead:

ysx_check_repeats(ids, spec, groups = c("ID", "TIME"), error_on_fail = FALSE)

Setting groups in the specification

ysx_regroup() removes all existing group settings and marks new ones. ysx_ungroup() removes them all. Both return a new specification.

regrouped <- ysx_regroup(spec, c("ID", "TIME"))
names(Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$dots$group), regrouped))
#> [1] "ID"   "TIME"

ungrouped <- ysx_ungroup(spec)
names(Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$dots$group), ungrouped))
#> character(0)

Within ysx_check(), the required number of rows per group comes from pre_grp_count in the dots of the group columns:

pre_grp_count Meaning
not set every group must have 1 row
a whole number n every group must have n rows
~, null, or None do not check repeats

All group columns that set it must agree.
